analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-010 (rules.json:746, AF-3-17): "o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr ... The occupancy estimate is the binary write pointer minus the binary read pointer ... it is pessimistic ... a value above the depth makes it never 1". So the estimate is assumed to stay in 0..DEPTH. With i_full_thr=DEPTH the estimate can reach 8 only when the FIFO is full, which gives contract CHK-013(c) (contract.json:524): "if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy)". Metastability model, spec 10.6.4 (spec:653, AF-10.6.4-01 rules.json:5481): "Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent. When a bit changes at the input of the last stage, the model chooses ... an extra delay of 0, 1, or 2 destination cycles ... If the input changes again while a change is pending, the pending value is replaced". spec:684 then claims: "A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value for a while instead of the new one." CHK-014 (contract.json:559) is meant to run with the model off. The test logs NNC_NOT_VERIFIABLE (base.s1.log:48) and runs it with the model on.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:120 w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s (4-bit, unclamped); :106 w_full_n = (reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ 4'b1100); :125-126 o_full = blk|w_full_n, o_full_thr = (w_occ >= i_full_thr). For o_full_thr=1 with o_full=0 at i_full_thr=8, w_occ must be 9..15, so w_rgray_s must hold a value the read pointer never had together with the current write pointer. The source of such values is m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-179 and :182: each bit has its own random extra delay (0..2 cycles), so a later Gray update on bit B can reach the output before an earlier, still-pending update on bit A. Example consistent with the log: the read pointer goes 1→2→3 (Gray 0001→0011→0010). The bit-1 rise gets +2 cycles and the bit-0 fall gets +0, so w_rgray_s=0000 (binary 0). With reg_wbin=9 (Gray 1101): w_occ=9≥8 → o_full_thr=1, and 1101≠1100 → o_full=0. This is exactly the failing sample. The failing clock setting is wr 14 ns / rd 6 ns (base.s1.log:47): the read pointer changes 2+ times per write period, which makes such overtaking likely. The same 20 tests pass with the plain chain: model_off.s1.log:175 'TESTS=20 PASS=20' and syn.s1.log:174 'PASS=20', both with CHK-013 fails=0 (model_off.s1.log:235, syn.s1.log:224).

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model follows spec 10.6.4 word for word (independent per-bit delay 0..2 with pending replacement, spec:653). The spec's own justification at spec:684 ('a late bit makes the destination see the previous pointer value') only holds if consecutive pointer updates are more than 2 destination cycles apart. The figures deliberately space them 'six source cycles apart' (spec:653). Under normal traffic that premise is false, and the model creates sync values that are neither the old nor the new pointer. This contradicts REQ-FUNC-010 ('above the depth makes it never 1'), REQ-FUNC-008/009 and TEST-008 'flags never optimistic' (rules.json:8782). All failing runs have the model on; model_off and syn pass.
candidates.evidence_against: The model is an RTL deliverable (FEAT-009, spec:93) and could be fixed without a spec change if the designer reads 'models the extra delay caused by metastability' as the binding intent and the per-bit wording as an implementation detail.

candidates.evidence_for: m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv (rtl/) is the unit that produces non-physical values: a real 2-FF chain can only resolve the one bit that changed within the setup/hold aperture. Here a bit that changed earlier can come out later than a bit that changed after it (lines 158-177). The FIFO core (wr/rd) is clean with the plain chain (model_off, syn: 20/20 pass, CHK-013=0). The core also has no clamp on w_occ (wr.sv:120,126), so an out-of-range estimate becomes visible on o_full_thr.
candidates.evidence_against: The model does what spec 10.6.4 asks. Adding a clamp to the core would hide the symptom but not fix the cause, because a read pointer that appears to run ahead could also make o_full optimistic. The Cummings-style core logic is correct for any physically possible synchronizer output.

candidates.evidence_for: The test runs CHK-014 with the model on although the contract wants it off (contract.json:559 'With the metastability model off'). It notes this as NNC_NOT_VERIFIABLE (base.s1.log:48) but still applies all always-on checks.
candidates.evidence_against: The failing check is CHK-013, which applies in every run and comes straight from the contract (contract.json:524) and REQ-FUNC-010. The expected value is derived correctly. The same failure appears in CHK-015/016/017/018/020, which are meant to run with the model.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify spec 10.6.4 and fix the model (A+C): the model must only ever output a value the source vector really had, in order. Ways to do that: (a) apply the extra delay only to a bit whose input changed within a small window before the capturing edge, using $realtime (per-bit, keeps DEC-039 because m_vlsit_afifo_sync still has only instances); (b) cap the delay so that a pending change is committed before a later change of any bit of the same vector can be shown, which needs a vector-level model and therefore a spec change to DEC-039/10.6.4; (c) state in the spec that per-bit skew must not exceed the minimum spacing of source updates, and enforce it in the model. Re-run base.s1-s5 after the fix. (2) If the designer keeps the model as specified, the spec must say what the FIFO core must do with incoherent sync values (e.g. clamp w_occ to DEPTH, treat out-of-range values as full/empty) and update REQ-FUNC-010; then the RTL core (wr.sv:120-126, rd.sv:112-118) has to change. (3) Test: optionally run CHK-014 only with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 as the contract says. This does not change CHK-013 and is not a fix for the root cause.

analyses.spec_says: CHK-023 (contract.json:757-758): 'Part 2: start another sequence and assert only i_rst_n_wr in the middle of it. Part 3: ... assert only i_rst_n_rd ... The handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked. After each of parts 2 and 3, reset both domains'. Spec DEC-031 (spec:1498) / spec:436: 'If only one domain gets a hardware reset during a software reset, the handshake can wait forever ...; the IP does not repair it'. ERR-003 (spec:1099): 'Reset asserted in one domain only, after the FIFO was used | FIFO state inconsistent; not detected'. ASM-005 (spec:1461). On the other side, CHK-013 (contract.json:524) applies 'At every rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_rst_n_wr=1', with no exemption.
analyses.rtl_does: After a write-only hardware reset, reg_wbin/reg_wgray go to 0 (wr.sv:141-154) and the write FSM goes to RUN with req_wr=0 (wr.sv:193-221). If the read side has not yet reset its pointer through RST, or never saw the short request, its pointer stays at the post-part-1 value. The write side then synchronizes that non-zero read pointer, so w_occ = 0 - rbin_s wraps (e.g. 15) ≥ 8 → o_full_thr=1, while w_full_n=0 → o_full=0 (wr.sv:120,126). The read side likewise has rgray≠wgray_s → o_empty=0 with nothing written (rd.sv:97,117). This matches the paired SVA CHK-005/CHK-006 read-edge failures at 83339/83353/83367 ns, 14 ns apart, just before this failure (cell3.s1.log:262-267). The request is held only ~3 write cycles before the write reset (test :1187-1191). With S=3/4 (cell3/cell4) plus the model, the read side may not have finished its reset before the request is wiped, which explains why only cell3/cell4 fail. No waveform is available to confirm exactly which part (2 or 3) produced the sample.

The CHK-013 block in _on_w (:190-204) is gated only by v['aw'] and stays active during the 20-cycle window after a one-domain reset. Expected exp = full&sw&!busy = 0 (:201), got 1.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec explicitly declares the state after a one-domain reset inconsistent and not repaired (ERR-003 spec:1099, DEC-031 spec:436/1498). The contract says that window is 'not checked' (contract.json:758). The test already disables its scoreboard there (:1190, :1211) but leaves CHK-013 (:196-204) armed during widle(20) (:1199, :1221). analyses.options: Same as test_chk_014/016: redefine the metastability model (spec 10.6.4 + cell_sync.sv) so the synchronized vector is always a value the source held, in order. Or define and implement out-of-range handling in the core. Keep CHK-003 unchanged.

analyses.spec_says: Contract CHK-005 (contract.json:342): '... On an assertion of i_rst_n_wr or i_rst_n_rd, Q and P are cleared and checking stops until both resets are released.' Contract CHK-023 (contract.json:758): 'The handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked. After each of parts 2 and 3, reset both domains'. Spec ERR-003 (spec:1099): 'Reset asserted in one domain only ... FIFO state inconsistent; not detected'. DEC-031 (spec:1498), ASM-005 (spec:1461).
analyses.rtl_does: After a hardware reset of only the write domain (or only the read domain) during a software reset, the two pointers are no longer consistent (wr.sv:141-154 reset reg_wbin/reg_wgray only; rd.sv:133-146 reset only the read pointer). The other side keeps its pointer, so rd.sv:97/117 can give o_empty=0 with no word written, and o_rd_data shows old storage. All 13 fails fall inside test_chk_023_hw_reset_during_sw_reset: base.s4 96714000 (test 023 window 95078-97154 ns, base.s4.log:92-96); cell3 83339000-83411000 (test 023 started 82354 ns, failed at 83377 ns; cell3.s1.log:130-144, 262-273); cell4 90533000-90605000 (cell4.s1.log:130-144); rd_slow 102039000/102053000 (test 023 100396-102493 ns). The fails are paired with CHK-006 at the same times and come every read period (14 ns), i.e. o_empty=0 on consecutive read edges with an empty reference. model_off/syn: 0 fails (model_off.s1.log:236, syn.s1.log:225), because with the plain 2-FF chain the read side finishes RST before the write-only reset.
analyses.test_does: SVA nnc_chk_sb.sv:56-101: Q/P are cleared while either reset is low, and chk_act is set back to 1 as soon as both resets are high (:67-97). a_CHK_005 (:104-106) then requires o_rd_data == head and P/Q non-empty whenever o_empty=0. There is no exemption for the one-domain-reset window, unlike the Python model (sb_on=False at test :1190, :1211) and unlike nnc_chk_wr.sv:74-79 (rd_only_rst hand fix for CHK-011). Stimulus test_async_gray_fifo.py:1182-1222: one-domain resets, then 20 idle write cycles before hw_reset.

candidates.evidence_for: All 13 fails are inside test_chk_023, in the window the contract says is 'not checked' and the spec says is inconsistent (ERR-003). The Python scoreboard is disabled there, but the SVA scoreboard re-arms (nnc_chk_sb.sv:96 chk_act<=1) as soon as the single reset is released. The wr checker already has the equivalent exemption for CHK-011 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:74-79).
candidates.evidence_against: The fails depend on the model/cell (none in model_off/syn/base.s1-s3). Whether the read side was caught un-reset depends on crossing latency, so an exact waveform has not been examined.

candidates.evidence_for: CHK-005's re-arm rule ('until both resets are released', contract.json:342) literally re-enables checking after a one-domain reset. That contradicts CHK-023 'not checked' and ERR-003. The checker implements CHK-005 literally.
candidates.evidence_against: CHK-023 and ERR-003 are explicit, so the intent is clear. Only the CHK-005 wording lacks the carve-out.

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL makes no attempt to restore consistency after a single-domain reset.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec explicitly says the IP does not repair it (DEC-031 spec:436, ERR-003 spec:1099). Not an RTL requirement.

analyses.options: Fix checker: in nnc_chk_sb.sv keep chk_act=0 after a reset of only one domain until a reset that covers both domains has been seen, mirroring rd_only_rst in nnc_chk_wr.sv:74-79 and the Python sb_on handling (test :1190, :1211). Clarify the contract: add to CHK-005/CHK-006 'checking does not restart after a reset of only one domain until both domains have been reset' (consistent with ERR-003/CHK-023). No RTL change unless the spec is changed to require recovery from a one-domain reset.

analyses.failure: CHK-006 (assertion) — flags never optimistic: 13 fails, first at 96714000
analyses.spec_says: Contract CHK-006 (contract.json:365): '(b) At every rising edge of i_clk_rd with i_rst_n_rd=1: if N == 0 and P is empty, then o_empty=1'. N/P come from the CHK-005 model, which 'stops until both resets are released' (contract.json:342). CHK-023 (contract.json:758): 'The handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked'. ERR-003 (spec:1099): FIFO state inconsistent after a one-domain reset.
analyses.rtl_does: Same as CHK-005. After a one-domain hardware reset in test_chk_023, the read pointer and the synchronized write pointer disagree, so o_empty = (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s) is 0 (rd.sv:97,117) while nothing has been written since the checker cleared Q/P. Fails occur at the same timestamps as CHK-005 (base.s4 96714000; cell3 83339000-83411000; cell4 90533000-90605000; rd_slow 102039000/102053000), all in test_chk_023 windows. 0 fails in model_off/syn (model_off.s1.log:237, syn.s1.log:226).
analyses.test_does: nnc_chk_sb.sv:118-121 a_CHK_006_rd: (chk_act && i_rst_n_wr && q_n==0 && p_n==0) |-> o_empty==1, where chk_act re-arms right after both resets are high (:96). No one-domain-reset exemption.

candidates.evidence_for: Same as CHK-005. All fails are in the contract's 'not checked' window after a one-domain reset (CHK-023). The SVA lacks the exemption the Python scoreboard has (test :1190, :1211).
candidates.evidence_against: Depends on crossing latency/seed. Exact cycle not confirmed by waveform.

candidates.evidence_for: The CHK-005/006 re-arm wording conflicts with CHK-023 and ERR-003.
candidates.evidence_against: Intent in CHK-023/ERR-003 is explicit.

candidates.evidence_for: o_empty=0 with nothing written is an optimistic flag in isolation.
candidates.evidence_against: Spec declares the post-one-domain-reset state inconsistent and not repaired (DEC-031, ERR-003).

analyses.options: Same as CHK-005: keep the SVA scoreboard disarmed after a one-domain reset until both domains have been reset, and/or clarify contract CHK-005/006 re-arm wording. No RTL change without a spec change.

analyses.failure: CHK-012 (assertion) — write-domain outputs change only at i_clk_wr edges: 11 fails, first at 111833000
analyses.spec_says: Contract CHK-012 (contract.json:509): 'o_full and o_full_thr change only in the time step of a rising edge of i_clk_wr, of an assertion of i_rst_n_wr, or of a change of i_rst_n_sw'. Port type LVL-STS (AF-6.2-06, rules.json:2880): 'It changes after a clock edge ..., never between edges except for the effect of the static thresholds'. REQ-FUNC-010 (rules.json:746): 'The thresholds are static: they are written once before the FIFO is used and do not change while it is in use.' o_full_thr is a 'Combinational function of i_full_thr and the pointers' (contract.json:82).
analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:126 o_full_thr = (w_occ >= i_full_thr) is combinational in i_full_thr, as specified. When the testbench changes i_full_thr between edges while i_rst_n_wr=1, o_full_thr changes immediately. Every fail is a few ns after a test boundary where the new test's threshold differs from the previous one. base.s1 111833000, ~5.6 ns after test_chk_032 starts at 111827.36 ns with full_thr=0 (sim.log:194-197; previous test full_thr=8, so the empty FIFO's o_full_thr 0→1). base.s2 115475000 (test_chk_030 start 115465.98 ns, after the random-threshold test_chk_029) and 120591000 (chk_032 start 120590.08). Also fails in model_off.s1 185662000 and syn.s1 185662000 (chk_032 start 185656.51), i.e. independent of the metastability model.
analyses.test_does: Env.start() (test_async_gray_fifo.py:146-149) writes the new test's idle values, including i_full_thr=self.ft, before calling hw_reset() (:160). At that moment i_rst_n_wr is still 1 from the previous test. test_chk_032 uses ft=0 for its first pair (:1660-1662). The SVA a_CHK_012 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:65-72, 115-118) compares the negedge snapshot with the posedge-sampled value and is disabled only while i_rst_n_wr=0, so the mid-cycle threshold change is flagged.

candidates.evidence_for: The stimulus changes the 'static' i_full_thr while the write domain is out of reset, i.e. while the FIFO is in use. This breaks REQ-FUNC-010 'written once before the FIFO is used' and the contract's own constraint ('thresholds are set before the reset release and never changed', contract.json:1029 note for AF-3-17). Fails occur only at test boundaries with a different threshold, in every configuration including model_off/syn.
candidates.evidence_against: The test infrastructure (Env.start) is shared, and the check could instead have an exception for threshold changes (see C).

candidates.evidence_for: AF-6.2-06 explicitly allows LVL-STS changes 'between edges ... for the effect of the static thresholds', but contract CHK-012 (contract.json:509) lists only clock edge, i_rst_n_wr assertion and i_rst_n_sw change as allowed causes.
candidates.evidence_against: REQ-FUNC-010 forbids changing the thresholds while in use. If the stimulus follows that, CHK-012 as written is correct.

candidates.evidence_for: None. A combinational o_full_thr is required by REQ-FUNC-018 (rules.json:1028) and contract.json:82.
candidates.evidence_against: Registering o_full_thr would violate REQ-FUNC-018 and the 'zero latency' threshold behaviour of CHK-032.

analyses.options: Fix test: in Env.start() assert both hardware resets (or call reset_dut) before driving the new i_full_thr/i_empty_thr, or drive the thresholds inside reset_dut while i_rst_n_wr=0, so thresholds only change while the domain is in reset, per REQ-FUNC-010/AF-3-17. Clarify contract (optional): add 'or a change of the static threshold i_full_thr' to CHK-012's list of allowed causes for o_full_thr, matching AF-6.2-06. This only states a spec-granted exception and does not weaken the other causes. No RTL change.

analyses.failure: CHK-013 (assertion) — o_full_thr consistency: 55 fails, first at 1681000
analyses.spec_says: Contract CHK-013 (contract.json:524): '(c) if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy)'. REQ-FUNC-010 (rules.json:746): o_full_thr = estimate ≥ i_full_thr, 'a value above the depth makes it never 1'. Model definition spec:653 (AF-10.6.4-01) vs spec:684 claim. ERR-003 (spec:1099) for one-domain resets.
analyses.rtl_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:122-128 checks this at every i_clk_wr edge. RTL wr.sv:120 (w_occ unclamped), :106 (full = exact Gray match), :126 (o_full_thr = w_occ >= i_full_thr). The failure needs w_occ > DEPTH with no full match, i.e. an incoherent synchronized read pointer. Two sources: (1) most fails come from the per-bit independent extra delay of the simulation model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182), which lets a later Gray bit overtake an earlier pending one. All base/cell/macro/small/wr_slow/rd_slow runs (model on) fail, while model_off and syn have CHK-013 fails=0 (model_off.s1.log:235, syn.s1.log:224). Per-run failure counts are 4-6 (e.g. base.s1.log:302 fails=4, base.s4.log:275 fails=6). Fail times match the Python CHK-013 failures in tests 014/015/017/018/020/024 (e.g. sim.log:249-253). (2) In cell3/cell4, some fails fall in test_chk_023 after a one-domain hardware reset, where spec ERR-003 says the pointer state is inconsistent (cell3.s1.log:134, 148).
analyses.test_does: SVA a_CHK_013 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:123-127), disabled only while i_rst_n_wr=0. No exemption for the one-domain-reset window. The Python mirror is test_async_gray_fifo.py:196-204.

candidates.evidence_for: Most fails depend only on the model being enabled. The model follows spec:653 literally, but the spec's reasoning at spec:684 (a late bit only shows the previous value) is false for closely spaced updates. That contradicts REQ-FUNC-010 'above the depth makes it never 1' and TEST-008 'flags never optimistic' (rules.json:8782).
candidates.evidence_against: The model file could be fixed as an RTL deliverable without a spec change (A).

candidates.evidence_for: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:158-177 produces synchronized vectors that a physical synchronizer cannot produce. The core has no clamp on w_occ (wr.sv:120-126).
candidates.evidence_against: The core is correct with the plain chain and the synthesis cells (0 fails). The model matches the spec text.

candidates.evidence_for: The subset of fails in test_chk_023 (cell3/cell4) lies in the one-domain-reset window that CHK-023/ERR-003 say is not checked, and the assertion has no exemption there.
candidates.evidence_against: Most fails (tests 014/015/016-018/020/024) are in normal both-domain operation, where CHK-013 follows directly from REQ-FUNC-010.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify spec 10.6.4 and fix m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv so the model only outputs values the source vector really held, in order: randomise only the bit that changed within a small window before the capturing edge, or enforce vector-level ordering (needs a DEC-039 change). (2) Alternatively, specify and implement out-of-range handling of the occupancy estimate in wr.sv:120-126 / rd.sv:112-118 (spec change to REQ-FUNC-010). (3) For the test_chk_023 subset: add a one-domain-reset exemption window to the SVA (like rd_only_rst in nnc_chk_wr.sv:74-79) and the Python check, per CHK-023/ERR-003. Do not relax CHK-013(c) in normal operation.
